title: Minimax equality on convex compact sets
statement:
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ and let $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$. Suppose that $X$ and $Y$ are nonempty, that $X$ is compact and convex, that $Y$ is convex, that the map $x \mapsto f(x,y)$ is continuous and convex on $X$ for every $y \in Y$, that the map $y \mapsto f(x,y)$ is concave on $Y$ for every $x \in X$, and that $f$ is bounded above and below on $X \times Y$. Suppose moreover that for every nonempty finite subset $u \subseteq X$,
\[
  \inf_{x \in X} \sup_{y \in Y} f(x,y) \;\le\; \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in u} f(x,y),
\]
and that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists a nonempty finite subset $u \subseteq X$ with
\[
  \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in u} f(x,y) \;\le\; \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in X} f(x,y) + \varepsilon.
\]
Then
\[
  \inf_{x \in X} \sup_{y \in Y} f(x,y) \;=\; \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in X} f(x,y).
\]
hypotheses_covered: f(·,y) continuous on X for each y in Y
f(·,y) convex on X for each y in Y
f(x,·) concave on Y for each x in X
for every nonempty finite u ⊆ X, the full upper value is ≤ the finite-sample lower value
for every ε>0 some nonempty finite u ⊆ X makes its lower value within ε of the full lower value
replaced:
If the standard convex-compact minimax hypotheses hold, the finite no-regret bound
$\texttt{OnlineLearning.Theorem71FiniteNoRegretBound}$ holds, and the compact approximation
property $\texttt{OnlineLearning.Theorem71CompactApproximation}$ holds, then the minimax
equality
\[
  \inf_{x \in X} \sup_{y \in Y} f(x,y)
    = \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in X} f(x,y)
\]
holds.
